In botany and dendrology , a rhizome ( / ˈ r aɪ z oʊ m / RY -zohm ) [ note 1 ] is a modified subterranean plant stem that sends out roots and shoots from its nodes . Rhizomes are also called creeping rootstalks or just rootstalks . [ 3 ] Rhizomes develop from axillary buds and grow horizontally. The rhizome also retains the ability to allow new shoots to grow upwards. [ 4 ]
